newsitem.title: USA: Albany County, NY Airport gets approval for bonds.
newsitem.headline: Albany County, NY Airport gets approval for bonds.

text.p: The Albany County, New York Airport Authority on Wednesday said that the county comptroller, who had wanted it to sell $100 million of bonds on a competitive basis, had agreed to a negotiated sale.
The sale still must be approved by the Authority's board, which will meet on February 3, a spokesman for the Authority said.
He added that if the board gives the deal its go-ahead, the bonds probably would be sold around February 12 or February 13.

The Albany County comptroller had objected to the sale because he thought that a competitive offering would be less costly, although the Authority argued that as a first-time issuer, having the issues sold through negotiation likely would produce a better result.
The syndicate is led by Lehman Brothers.

As part of the agreement with the county comptroller, the term of the bonds was reduced by three years to 27 years, and local residents will be able to buy the bonds through a presale order period, the Authority's spokesman said.

"We are satisfied with the components of the agreement that was reached yesterday between the staff of the Authority and the Albany County Comptroller," the Authority's chief executive officer, John Egan, said in prepared remarks.
